newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain 6-mo yld seen at new low when issues resume.
newsitem.headline: Spain 6-mo yld seen at new low when issues resume.

text.p: The Spanish Treasury will resume issuance on Wednesday of its six-month bills after a year-long hiatus, and dealers and analysts believe appetite for the paper will be strong given the outlook for declining rates.
Conservative money market and investment funds are expected to snap up a large amount of six-month T-bills, betting on a swift reduction in the official 7.25-percent money market rate.

"Treasury used to offer six month bills when it had difficulties in the funding process. But this does not seem to be the case now," a dealer said, adding that the Treasury is just offering what the market wanted to buy.
Analysts expect the sale to result in record low six-month yields of between 6.84 and 6.88 percent, in line with today's grey market.
At the last auction in August 1995, six-month paper yielded 9.407 percent. The record low on this instrument was set on August 1994 at 7.93 percent.
At the most recent one-year bill sale in August, this longer-term paper registered a record low yield of 6.954 percent.
The Bank of Spain left its official rate unchanged this morning, but the market is expecting a 25-basis point reduction at the October 3 tender after the 1997 budget.
